steps.name: the runner really is a graphical login session
launch TextEdit
steps.comment: `open` goes through LaunchServices, which needs no Apple Events authorisation. `tell application "TextEdit" to activate` would raise a modal and block.

steps.name: new document, with a keystroke rather than an Apple Event
the document window really exists
steps.exec: osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to count windows of process "TextEdit"'

steps.name: both lines landed, so Return was not swallowed
steps.comment: Read through System Events, not `tell application "TextEdit"`. Talking to the app directly needs Apple Events authorisation and blocks on a modal; System Events does not.
steps.exec: osascript -e 'with timeout of 20 seconds' -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "TextEdit" to get value of text area 1 of scroll area 1 of window 1' -e 'end timeout' | tr '\r' '\n' | grep -c . | tr -d ' '
